bottom_line: In PARADIGM-HF, LCZ696 versus enalapril reduced the primary composite of death from cardiovascular causes or first hospitalization for heart failure (hazard ratio, 0.80; 95% CI, 0.73 to 0.87).
implications: These data support that, in this trial population, LCZ696 compared with enalapril lowered the risk of the primary composite outcome (21.8% vs. 26.5%; hazard ratio 0.80, 95% CI 0.73–0.87) and all-cause death (17.0% vs. 19.8%; hazard ratio 0.84, 95% CI 0.76–0.93). The findings do not establish benefit for outcomes that were not statistically different (e.g., new-onset atrial fibrillation 3.1% vs. 3.1%; hazard ratio 0.97, 95% CI 0.72–1.31).

harms.text: Symptomatic hypotension occurred more often with LCZ696 than enalapril.
Elevated serum creatinine ≥2.5 mg/dl occurred less often with LCZ696 than enalapril.
Cough occurred less often with LCZ696 than enalapril.
Angioedema confirmed by blinded adjudication occurred in 19 patients with LCZ696 and 10 with enalapril; no airway compromise.
harms.quote: Angio- edema was confirmed by blinded adjudication in 19 patients in the LCZ696 group and in 10 patients in the enalapril group (P = 0.13). No patient had airway compromise or required mechanical air- way protection.

harms.text: Fewer patients on LCZ696 stopped study medication because of an adverse event (10.7% vs 12.3%).

inclusion_criteria.quote: Eligibility requirements at screening included an age of at least 18 years

inclusion_criteria.text: NYHA class II, III, or IV symptoms
inclusion_criteria.quote: Eligibility requirements at screening included an age of at least 18 years, New York Heart Association (NYHA) class II, III, or IV symptoms

inclusion_criteria.text: Ejection fraction of 40% or less (changed to 35% or less by amendment)
inclusion_criteria.quote: an ejection fraction of 40% or less (which was changed to 35% or less by an amendment to the protocol on December 15, 2010)

inclusion_criteria.text: BNP at least 150 pg/ml or NT-proBNP ≥600 pg/ml; or if hospitalized for HF within prior 12 months, BNP at least 100 pg/ml or NT-proBNP ≥400 pg/ml
inclusion_criteria.quote: Patients were required to have a plasma B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) level of at least 150 pg per milliliter (or an N-terminal pro-BNP [NT-proBNP] level ≥600 pg per milliliter) or, if they had been hospitalized for heart failure within the previous 12 months, a BNP of at least 100 pg per milliliter (or an NT-proBNP ≥400 pg per milliliter).

inclusion_criteria.text: For at least 4 weeks before screening, stable dose of a beta-blocker and an ACE inhibitor (or ARB) equivalent to at least 10 mg of enalapril daily
inclusion_criteria.quote: for at least 4 weeks before screening, patients were required to take a stable dose of a beta-blocker and an ACE inhibitor (or ARB) equivalent to at least 10 mg of enalapril daily.
